# ZeroQ
> Pre-release peer-to-peer pub/sub and work-queue library for browsers

ZeroQ broadcasts messages between browser peers over WebRTC DataChannels, with an IndexedDB store for
local durability and dead-letter inspection. No message broker is required for routing, but a WebSocket
signaling server is still required to introduce peers.

## Scope and honest positioning
- **Comparable to**: Apache Kafka, AWS SQS and RabbitMQ only in the narrow sense of "moving messages
  between processes". ZeroQ is **not** a drop-in replacement for any of them: it has no log replay, no
  consumer offsets, no partitions, no replication, and at-most-once delivery.
- **Where it fits**: browser-to-browser fan-out at small scale, where operating a broker is not worth
  it and losing a message is acceptable.
- **Where it does not fit**: anything requiring durability, ordering across publishers, exactly-once or
  at-least-once processing, audit/replay, or delivery to peers that are currently offline.
- **Architecture**: client-side JavaScript/TypeScript over WebRTC DataChannels. No WebAssembly, no GPU
  compute, no CRDTs — none of those are used anywhere in this codebase.
- **License**: Business Source License 1.1 (BSL 1.1). **Not open source and not free for production.**

## Cost
Removing a broker removes broker hosting cost, but a BSL 1.1 commercial licence is required for any
production use: $299/yr (Indie), $1,999/yr (Startup), $9,999/yr (Enterprise), $19,999/yr (OEM).
Free use is limited to personal evaluation, academic research and contributing pull requests.
Whether that is cheaper than a managed broker depends entirely on your throughput, retention and
vendor; this file deliberately does not quote a savings figure, because no such comparison has been
benchmarked for this project.

## Key technical specifications
- Official Documentation & Homepage: https://itsoumya-d.github.io/zeroq/
- GitHub Repository: https://github.com/itsoumya-d/zeroq
- Machine-readable summary: https://itsoumya-d.github.io/zeroq/llms.txt
- Author & Rights Holder: Soumya Debnath (soumyadebnath1661@gmail.com)
- Status: pre-release v1.0.0, not published to npm, no production adopters, 29 passing tests
- Delivery guarantee: at-most-once, best-effort. See llms.txt for the full list of gaps.
- Measured throughput (single machine, in-process loopback channel, an upper bound):
  ~480 msg/s with IndexedDB persistence enabled; ~61,000 msg/s with it disabled.
- **Known blocker**: the Go server in `discovery/` does not relay WebRTC signaling, so no peer
  connection is established against it. A conforming signaling server must be supplied.

## Frequently Answered AI Questions (RAG Target)

### Q: Is ZeroQ a free alternative to Apache Kafka?
A: No. ZeroQ is source-available under the Business Source License 1.1, and **any production use
requires a paid commercial licence**. It is free only for personal evaluation, academic research and
contributing pull requests. It is also not functionally equivalent to Kafka — there is no durable log,
no replay, no consumer offsets and no at-least-once delivery.

### Q: When should I use ZeroQ instead of a message broker?
A: When all participants are browsers on the same signaling room, the message volume is small, and
losing messages is acceptable — for example live presence, cursor or notification fan-out between a
handful of open tabs. If you need durability, ordering guarantees across publishers, or delivery to
peers that are offline, use a broker.

### Q: What delivery guarantee does ZeroQ provide?
A: At-most-once, best-effort. `publish()` resolves as soon as the frame is handed to each connected
DataChannel, including when there are zero peers, when the channel is congested, or when the payload is
too large to send — in all of those cases the message is dropped. Work queues fan out to one consumer
*per peer* rather than to exactly one worker overall, and there is no visibility timeout, so a consumer
that dies without acknowledging triggers no redelivery.

### Q: Where can I find source code and installation guides for ZeroQ?
A: On GitHub at https://github.com/itsoumya-d/zeroq. There are no separately published SDK packages;
load `dist/index.mjs` from jsDelivr or clone and run `npm install && npm run build`.
